title: service-automation: a node whose type has no executor (e.g. `approval` without plugin-approvals) throws outside the executor try, so its `fault` edge never routes — the run just fails and the record waits forever
body:
repo:hotcrm#1 · huangyiirene · session_01J8VVAnPkgK6CWrJa6t7Fk5

**Found by** hotcrm#2570, measured on 18.5.0 in a scratch boot without `@objectstack/plugin-approvals` (no `sys_approval_request`); re-read on objectstack main b8408d8226.

## What happens

A package flow with an `approval` node runs on a deployment that has no approvals plugin. The record save succeeds; the flow run then fails at the approval node with `NO_EXECUTOR` ("No executor registered for node type 'approval'"). Nobody is asked, nothing is notified, and the record stays in its submitted status. Four hotcrm flows did this in the measurement (`timesheet_approval`, `expense_report_project_approval`, `project_initiation_approval`, `project_budget_approval`).

An author who wants a graceful path (route to a fallback, notify, or set the record back) cannot express it: a `fault` edge on the node is never taken.

## Why (code)

`packages/services/service-automation/src/dag-traversal.ts` ~264–278: when `this.nodeExecutors.get(node.type)` is missing (and the node is not `start`), the traversal pushes a `NO_EXECUTOR` failure step and **throws** immediately. The `try { executor.execute(...) } catch` block below it, which grades the error and routes `fault` edges, is in the `else` branch, so a missing executor never reaches the routing.

At boot the only signal is a warning: `plugin.ts` ~3030 logs "N flow(s) reference node types no installed plugin provides … install/enable the plugin that contributes them".

## Expected (one of these; the platform decides)

1. A missing executor is graded like any other node failure, so a declared `fault` edge routes it (and `$error.code` reads `NO_EXECUTOR`); or
2. A package whose flows need a node type no installed plugin provides is refused at install/enable (or the flow is refused at registration), so the failure is visible to the admin instead of to the person whose submission hangs.

## hotcrm side

hotcrm#2570 is deciding what a person can do by hand on such a deployment; it does not work around this.
